title: Naturality and rationalization of a completed tensor comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $p\in A$, and $\mathcal D$ an $A$-linear category [def-weil-linear-category]. Let $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal D$ be a full $A$-linear subcategory and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be an $A$-linear functor with natural unit $\eta_X:X\to LX$ such that composition with $\eta_X$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(LX,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(X,Y)$ for every $Y\in\mathcal C$. The inclusion in $\mathcal D$ is suppressed. Let $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$ be an $A$-linear equivalence restricting to an equivalence $P$ of $\mathcal C$. Suppose given isomorphisms $c_X:H(LX)\xrightarrow{\sim}L(HX)$ satisfying $H(\eta_X);c_X=\eta_{HX}$; naturality of $c$ is not assumed. Let $T:\mathcal D\times\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$ be a bifunctor whose morphism action is $A$-bilinear separately in its two arguments, and let $\tau_{X,Y}:H(T(X,Y))\xrightarrow{\sim}T(HX,HY)$ be a natural isomorphism. Define $B(M,N)=L(T(M,N))$ on $\mathcal C$ and $d_{M,N}=c_{T(M,N)};L(\tau_{M,N})$.

The family $c$ is natural in $X$, and $d$ is natural simultaneously in $M,N$. Use raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], with functor $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[1/p]$. Suppose $\bar P$ and $\bar B$ are functors on the localized category with the same object maps as $P,B$ and morphism formulas $\bar P(f/p^r)=P(f)/p^r$ and $\bar B(f/p^r,g/p^s)=B(f,g)/p^{r+s}$. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\bar\mu_{M,N}:\bar P\bar B(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar B(\bar P M,\bar P N)$$
whose component on every pair of integral objects is $Q(d_{M,N})$. Its inverse has component $Q(d_{M,N}^{-1})$. No torsion-freeness of the Hom modules is required.

proof.text: Use diagrammatic composition $a;b=b\circ a$. The unit equation gives $H(\eta_X)=\eta_{HX};c_X^{-1}$. If $Y\in\mathcal C$ and $a,b:H(LX)\to Y$ satisfy $H(\eta_X);a=H(\eta_X);b$, then $\eta_{HX};c_X^{-1};a=\eta_{HX};c_X^{-1};b$. Both $c_X^{-1};a$ and $c_X^{-1};b$ have source $L(HX)$ and target $Y$, so the assumed Hom bijection for $HX,Y$ gives their equality. Composing on the left with $c_X$ gives $a=b$. This is cancellation only against targets in $\mathcal C$.

proof.text:
For $f:X\to X'$, put $a=H(Lf);c_{X'}$ and $b=c_X;L(Hf)$, arrows $H(LX)\to L(HX')$. Naturality of $\eta$ and the two unit equations give
$$H(\eta_X);a=H(\eta_X;Lf);c_{X'}=H(f);H(\eta_{X'});c_{X'}=H(f);\eta_{HX'},$$
$$H(\eta_X);b=\eta_{HX};L(Hf)=H(f);\eta_{HX'}.$$
Since $L(HX')\in\mathcal C$, Step 1 gives $H(Lf);c_{X'}=c_X;L(Hf)$. This proves naturality of the given $c$, without having assumed it.

proof.text:
For $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$ in $\mathcal C$, abbreviate $U=T(M,N)$, $U'=T(M',N')$, $h=T(f,g)$ and $k=T(Hf,Hg)$. The components $c_U$ and $L(\tau_{M,N})$ are isomorphisms between objects of $\mathcal C$: $H$ preserves $\mathcal C$, $L$ takes values there, and fullness lets us regard these arrows and inverses as arrows of $\mathcal C$. By Step 2 and the given naturality equation $H(h);\tau_{M',N'}=\tau_{M,N};k$,
$$P(B(f,g));d_{M',N'}=H(Lh);c_{U'};L(\tau_{M',N'})=c_U;L(Hh;\tau_{M',N'})=d_{M,N};L(k)=d_{M,N};B(Pf,Pg).$$
Here only preservation of composition by $L$ is used in the middle equality. This is simultaneous naturality of $d$.

proof.text: For each $M,M'\in\mathcal C$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] to the $A$-module $V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(M,M')$ and $p\in A$. Together with [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], it identifies the raw Hom module $V\otimes_A A[1/p]$ with fractions $f/p^r$, and every arrow has such a representative. No injectivity of $V\to V[1/p]$ is asserted: equality of $f/p^r$ and $f'/p^{r'}$ means $p^k(p^{r'}f-p^rf')=0$ for some $k\geq0$. From the composition rule in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], composition of fractions is $(f/p^r);(g/p^s)=(f;g)/p^{r+s}$: represent the two arrows by $f\otimes p^{-r}$ and $g\otimes p^{-s}$ and multiply their coefficients.

source.place: Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), 07JZ (definition-localization-module); specialization to each Hom module and raw bilinear composition

proof.text:
Define $\bar\mu_{M,N}=Q(d_{M,N})$. Every localized object is an object of $\mathcal C$, so this defines every component with the required source and target. For arbitrary localized arrows $u:M\to M'$ and $v:N\to N'$, choose $u=f/p^r$, $v=g/p^s$ using Step 4. The stipulated formulas for $\bar P,\bar B$ and localized composition [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] give
$$\bar P(\bar B(u,v));Q(d_{M',N'})=\frac{P(B(f,g));d_{M',N'}}{p^{r+s}}=\frac{d_{M,N};B(Pf,Pg)}{p^{r+s}}=Q(d_{M,N});\bar B(\bar P(u),\bar P(v)).$$
The middle equality is Step 3, mapped into the localized Hom module. Thus the family is natural on all pairs of localized arrows. The calculation starts with arbitrary chosen representatives of existing arrows and proves equality in the localization; it never cancels a power of $p$ in an integral Hom module.

proof.text: Since $Q$ is a functor [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], the arrows $Q(d_{M,N})$ and $Q(d_{M,N}^{-1})$ compose in either order to the corresponding identity. The inverse family is natural: multiply the naturality equation of Step 5 on the left by $Q(d_{M,N}^{-1})$ and on the right by $Q(d_{M',N'}^{-1})$ and use those two identity equations. The two families therefore form a natural isomorphism with the stated inverse. Any competing natural isomorphism satisfying the component formula has the same forward arrow at every object pair, because raw scalar localization adds no objects; hence it is equal to this one. All calculations remain valid for torsion Hom modules.
